newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador evaluates press report of Peru attack plan.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador evaluates press report of Peru attack plan.

text.p: The Ecuadoran government said on Thursday it was trying to evaluate a newspaper report that neighbouring Peru was planning to provoke a border incident to resume last year's armed conflict.
"We are trying to confirm it, it is still a press report," Ecuador's Defence Minister Victor Manuel Bayas told reporters. "We are analysing the situation militarily to see what our position is."

Expreso, a newspaper from the Ecuadoran coastal city of Guayaquil, alleged that Lima was planning operation "Victoria" to resume the fighting over a disputed jungle border area in the Condor mountain range that erupted early last year.
"The plan involves provoking a serious military incident in the Condor mountains ... and giving a rapid military response," said the newspaper.
In Lima, the Peruvian Foreign Ministry and defence sources flatly denied the newspaper report and confirmed that the peace process enjoyed "the goodwill of both countries."

The two Andean neighbours have been arguing about the Condor mountain borders for over a half a century. In 1942 they signed the Rio Protocol drawing up the borders -- which Ecuador insists is not valid and robbed it of half its Amazonian territory.
Tempers flare along the border each year around the anniversary of the treaty, but the Ecuadoran defence chief promised his troops would not provoke any incidents.
"We are keeping quiet. On the border our men are just doing their normal duties," said Bayas.
Peru's recent acknowledgment that it had bought a fleet of MiG-29 fighters caused concern in Ecuador and among the four guarantors of the Rio treaty -- the United States, Chile Brazil and Argentina.
